top_news.title: Star Health Brings
top_news.summary: PRNewswire Kolkata (West Bengal) [India], October 17: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited (NSE: STARHEALTH) (BSE: 543412), one of India's leading standalone health insurance companies, today announced the introduction of 'Bishram Grih' at select Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur. The first-of-its-kind initiative by Star Health offers pandal hoppers a comfortable lounge-style space to "Rest, Relax & Rejuvenate" during their Puja journey. Each Bishram Grih will also feature a technology-led Face Scan health assessment, enabling visitors to gain quick insights into select health indicators. Pandal hopping during Durga Puja can be tiring, particularly for those visiting multiple locations in a day. At each Bishram Grih, visitors can take a break, sit comfortably and enjoy refreshments such as tea and water before continuing their Puja journey. A key feature of the Bishram Grih is Star Health's Face Scan health assessment kiosk. Through a simple and contactless facial scan, visitors can receive an instant indicative health report covering approximately 17 health parameters. The assessment provides insights into select vital signs and indicators related to stress, recovery and heart rate variability, including heart rate, respiratory rate, stress index and HRV metrics, among others. Star Health will set up two Bishram Grihs in Kolkata and one in Durgapur. The initiative will be active from 16 October to 20 October 2026 at the following Puja pandals: - Bag bazar Sarbojanin Durgotsav Exhibition, Kolkata - 22 Palli Sarodotsab, Northern Park, Kolkata - Marconi Dakshina Pally, Durgapur Operating hours: 11AM onwards Commenting on the initiative, Mr. Himanshu Walia, Whole-time Director & CMO, Star Health Insurance, said, ""Durga Puja is a festival close to every Bengali's heart, and pandal hopping is an integral part of the celebrations. With thousands of people spending long hours visiting pandals, we wanted to create a space where they could pause, rest and recharge before continuing their Puja journey. Bishram Grih brings this thought to life by offering visitors a comfortable lounge-style space with refreshments at select pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur. By integrating a quick and contactless Face Scan health assessment into the experience, we are also encouraging visitors to become more aware of select health indicators in a simple and accessible manner. Through Bishram Grih, we hope to combine festive convenience with preventive health awareness and make wellbeing a meaningful part of the Durga Puja experience." Star Health also encourages pandal hoppers in Kolkata and Durgapur, particularly senior citizens and families with young children, to take precautions during the festivities. These include staying hydrated, taking regular breaks between pandal visits, wearing comfortable footwear and seeking medical advice in case of any discomfort. Commenting on the regional initiative, Mr. Atin Roy, Business Head - West Bengal, Star Health Insurance, said, "West Bengal comes alive during Durga Puja, with families and visitors spending long hours exploring pandals across the region. Bishram Grih responds to a practical need by offering pandal hoppers a comfortable space to pause, refresh and regain energy. Visitors can also access a complimentary, contactless Face Scan health assessment that provides an instant indicative report covering approximately 17 health parameters. By setting up these facilities at prominent pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur, we aim to make comfort and health awareness a meaningful part of the festive experience." By bringing together physical comfort and preventive health awareness, Bishram Grih seeks to make wellbeing a meaningful part of the Durga Puja experience. Through such technology-led initiatives, Star Health is exploring ways to complement health insurance protection with solutions that encourage people to remain more engaged with their overall wellbeing. About Star Health and Allied Insurance: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited (NSE: STARHEALTH) (BSE: 543412), one of India's leading standalone health insurance companies, commenced operations in 2006 as India's first standalone health insurance company. Star Health provides Health, Personal Accident and Travel Insurance to its customers. The Company has grown to emerge as one of the preferred health insurance companies in India with several pioneering products and services to its credit. With customer-centricity at its core, the Company has developed superior and innovative product offerings, service capabilities and a seamless claims management process. Star Health offers tailor-made products to cater to needs such as cancer, diabetes and cardiac illnesses, as well as specific segments such as senior citizens, women and children. Star Health is India's first health insurance company to settle over 1 crore claims. Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd. has a strong multi-channel distribution network of 900+ offices, over 8 lakh agents and robust bancassurance and financial institution partners. The Company has 15,000+ network hospitals and 18,500+ employees. Customers can call the number and press 1 for Home Healthcare or press 2 for planned hospitalisation. The service helps customers understand coverage, network hospital options, the cashless process, required documents and care pathways before admission or home-based treatment. top_news.title: Women
top_news.summary: Several women's organisations, including the All India Democratic Women's Association (AIDWA), the National Federation of Indian Women (NFIW), the All India Progressive Women's Association (AIPWA) and ALIFA, on Saturday held a joint protest march towards the Delhi Police headquarters against alleged sexual violence and police brutality against women during recent protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Speaking to ANI, Communist Party of India (CPI) leader Annie Raja said the protest against the alleged mistreatment of women was linked to the broader opposition to SIR and demands for the resignation of the CEC. We are into that protest because the vote chori is something in many ways; it is the biggest assault on women. So we are here; we were here every day protesting, demanding the cancellation of SIR and the resignation of CEC, she said. Alleging that women participating in the protests were being targeted to silence them and prevent them from occupying public spaces, Raja accused the Centre of using sexual assault as a weapon against women protesters. To silence us, to disappear the women of this country who are participating in the protest and occupying the public space, the fascist Amit Shah government or Modi government are using sexual assault as a weapon irrespective of age, she said. Raja alleged that women who had participated in the protests had been subjected to sexual assault and said the organisations would continue their demonstrations despite attempts to suppress them. Whatever may be your strategy to suppress us, oppress us, disappear us, the women of this country, we will come here, we will occupy the public space in hundred times more strength, she said. Demanding action against the police personnel allegedly responsible for the incidents, Raja said, We want the officials, the police who are responsible for using sexual assault as a weapon to silence and disappear women of this country from participating in the SIR protests; we want action against them. She also demanded the resignation of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, alleging that such actions by the police could not take place without his knowledge or orders. Amit Shah should resign because he is the Home Minister; without his knowledge and without his order, no police will dare to use sexual violence, sexual oppression and assaulting the women's private parts as a weapon to prevent women from taking part in the protest, she said. During the interaction, Raja also referred to the presence of Ankita Bhandari's parents at the protest. Meanwhile, the Delhi Police have registered multiple FIRs for alleged violations of prohibitory orders imposed in Connaught Place and other parts of New Delhi during protests on Friday, officials said on Saturday. According to police officials, announcements were repeatedly made asking people not to assemble, but a crowd gathered around Connaught Place. Police said FIRs would be registered for violations of prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and action would also be taken against repeat offenders. The action follows a Tiranga rally held by protesters outside Central Park in Connaught Place on Friday amid heightened security. Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) workers and supporters also gathered to hold a Tiranga rally, directing their protest against the Election Commission over alleged irregularities in the electoral process. In a related development, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke, who was detained by Delhi Police ahead of the planned 'Lehra Do Tiranga' rally in the national capital, will be produced before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) at Mandir Marg Police Station around 12 pm on Saturday, his legal counsel said. In a post on social media platform X, advocate Ratna Singh said, He will be produced before SEM Mandir Marg PS around 12 PM. Police placed Dipke under preventive detention at his residence in New Delhi on Friday, invoking prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS. CJP representatives alleged that he was taken to an undisclosed location without immediate access to his lawyers. The detention came amid heightened security arrangements and restrictions on public gatherings in parts of the national capital following protests over the electoral revision process and demands for action against the Election Commission. (ANI)

articles.title: Star Health Brings
articles.summary: PRNewswire Kolkata (West Bengal) [India], October 17: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited (NSE: STARHEALTH) (BSE: 543412), one of India's leading standalone health insurance companies, today announced the introduction of 'Bishram Grih' at select Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur. The first-of-its-kind initiative by Star Health offers pandal hoppers a comfortable lounge-style space to "Rest, Relax & Rejuvenate" during their Puja journey. Each Bishram Grih will also feature a technology-led Face Scan health assessment, enabling visitors to gain quick insights into select health indicators. Pandal hopping during Durga Puja can be tiring, particularly for those visiting multiple locations in a day. At each Bishram Grih, visitors can take a break, sit comfortably and enjoy refreshments such as tea and water before continuing their Puja journey. A key feature of the Bishram Grih is Star Health's Face Scan health assessment kiosk. Through a simple and contactless facial scan, visitors can receive an instant indicative health report covering approximately 17 health parameters. The assessment provides insights into select vital signs and indicators related to stress, recovery and heart rate variability, including heart rate, respiratory rate, stress index and HRV metrics, among others. Star Health will set up two Bishram Grihs in Kolkata and one in Durgapur. The initiative will be active from 16 October to 20 October 2026 at the following Puja pandals: - Bag bazar Sarbojanin Durgotsav Exhibition, Kolkata - 22 Palli Sarodotsab, Northern Park, Kolkata - Marconi Dakshina Pally, Durgapur Operating hours: 11AM onwards Commenting on the initiative, Mr. Himanshu Walia, Whole-time Director & CMO, Star Health Insurance, said, ""Durga Puja is a festival close to every Bengali's heart, and pandal hopping is an integral part of the celebrations. With thousands of people spending long hours visiting pandals, we wanted to create a space where they could pause, rest and recharge before continuing their Puja journey. Bishram Grih brings this thought to life by offering visitors a comfortable lounge-style space with refreshments at select pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur. By integrating a quick and contactless Face Scan health assessment into the experience, we are also encouraging visitors to become more aware of select health indicators in a simple and accessible manner. Through Bishram Grih, we hope to combine festive convenience with preventive health awareness and make wellbeing a meaningful part of the Durga Puja experience." Star Health also encourages pandal hoppers in Kolkata and Durgapur, particularly senior citizens and families with young children, to take precautions during the festivities. These include staying hydrated, taking regular breaks between pandal visits, wearing comfortable footwear and seeking medical advice in case of any discomfort. Commenting on the regional initiative, Mr. Atin Roy, Business Head - West Bengal, Star Health Insurance, said, "West Bengal comes alive during Durga Puja, with families and visitors spending long hours exploring pandals across the region. Bishram Grih responds to a practical need by offering pandal hoppers a comfortable space to pause, refresh and regain energy. Visitors can also access a complimentary, contactless Face Scan health assessment that provides an instant indicative report covering approximately 17 health parameters. By setting up these facilities at prominent pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur, we aim to make comfort and health awareness a meaningful part of the festive experience." By bringing together physical comfort and preventive health awareness, Bishram Grih seeks to make wellbeing a meaningful part of the Durga Puja experience. Through such technology-led initiatives, Star Health is exploring ways to complement health insurance protection with solutions that encourage people to remain more engaged with their overall wellbeing. articles.title: Star Health Brings
articles.summary: PRNewswire Kolkata (West Bengal) [India], October 17: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited (NSE: STARHEALTH) (BSE: 543412), one of India's leading standalone health insurance companies, today announced the introduction of 'Bishram Grih' at select Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur. The first-of-its-kind initiative by Star Health offers pandal hoppers a comfortable lounge-style space to "Rest, Relax & Rejuvenate" during their Puja journey. Each Bishram Grih will also feature a technology-led Face Scan health assessment, enabling visitors to gain quick insights into select health indicators. Pandal hopping during Durga Puja can be tiring, particularly for those visiting multiple locations in a day. At each Bishram Grih, visitors can take a break, sit comfortably and enjoy refreshments such as tea and water before continuing their Puja journey. A key feature of the Bishram Grih is Star Health's Face Scan health assessment kiosk. Through a simple and contactless facial scan, visitors can receive an instant indicative health report covering approximately 17 health parameters. The assessment provides insights into select vital signs and indicators related to stress, recovery and heart rate variability, including heart rate, respiratory rate, stress index and HRV metrics, among others. Star Health will set up two Bishram Grihs in Kolkata and one in Durgapur. The initiative will be active from 16 October to 20 October 2026 at the following Puja pandals: - Bag bazar Sarbojanin Durgotsav Exhibition, Kolkata - 22 Palli Sarodotsab, Northern Park, Kolkata - Marconi Dakshina Pally, Durgapur Operating hours: 11AM onwards Commenting on the initiative, Mr. Himanshu Walia, Whole-time Director & CMO, Star Health Insurance, said, ""Durga Puja is a festival close to every Bengali's heart, and pandal hopping is an integral part of the celebrations. With thousands of people spending long hours visiting pandals, we wanted to create a space where they could pause, rest and recharge before continuing their Puja journey. Bishram Grih brings this thought to life by offering visitors a comfortable lounge-style space with refreshments at select pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur. By integrating a quick and contactless Face Scan health assessment into the experience, we are also encouraging visitors to become more aware of select health indicators in a simple and accessible manner. Through Bishram Grih, we hope to combine festive convenience with preventive health awareness and make wellbeing a meaningful part of the Durga Puja experience." Star Health also encourages pandal hoppers in Kolkata and Durgapur, particularly senior citizens and families with young children, to take precautions during the festivities. These include staying hydrated, taking regular breaks between pandal visits, wearing comfortable footwear and seeking medical advice in case of any discomfort. Commenting on the regional initiative, Mr. Atin Roy, Business Head - West Bengal, Star Health Insurance, said, "West Bengal comes alive during Durga Puja, with families and visitors spending long hours exploring pandals across the region. Bishram Grih responds to a practical need by offering pandal hoppers a comfortable space to pause, refresh and regain energy. Visitors can also access a complimentary, contactless Face Scan health assessment that provides an instant indicative report covering approximately 17 health parameters. By setting up these facilities at prominent pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur, we aim to make comfort and health awareness a meaningful part of the festive experience." By bringing together physical comfort and preventive health awareness, Bishram Grih seeks to make wellbeing a meaningful part of the Durga Puja experience. Through such technology-led initiatives, Star Health is exploring ways to complement health insurance protection with solutions that encourage people to remain more engaged with their overall wellbeing. articles.title: Women
articles.summary: Several women's organisations, including the All India Democratic Women's Association (AIDWA), the National Federation of Indian Women (NFIW), the All India Progressive Women's Association (AIPWA) and ALIFA, on Saturday held a joint protest march towards the Delhi Police headquarters against alleged sexual violence and police brutality against women during recent protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Speaking to ANI, Communist Party of India (CPI) leader Annie Raja said the protest against the alleged mistreatment of women was linked to the broader opposition to SIR and demands for the resignation of the CEC. We are into that protest because the vote chori is something in many ways; it is the biggest assault on women. So we are here; we were here every day protesting, demanding the cancellation of SIR and the resignation of CEC, she said. Alleging that women participating in the protests were being targeted to silence them and prevent them from occupying public spaces, Raja accused the Centre of using sexual assault as a weapon against women protesters. To silence us, to disappear the women of this country who are participating in the protest and occupying the public space, the fascist Amit Shah government or Modi government are using sexual assault as a weapon irrespective of age, she said. Raja alleged that women who had participated in the protests had been subjected to sexual assault and said the organisations would continue their demonstrations despite attempts to suppress them. Whatever may be your strategy to suppress us, oppress us, disappear us, the women of this country, we will come here, we will occupy the public space in hundred times more strength, she said. Demanding action against the police personnel allegedly responsible for the incidents, Raja said, We want the officials, the police who are responsible for using sexual assault as a weapon to silence and disappear women of this country from participating in the SIR protests; we want action against them. She also demanded the resignation of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, alleging that such actions by the police could not take place without his knowledge or orders. Amit Shah should resign because he is the Home Minister; without his knowledge and without his order, no police will dare to use sexual violence, sexual oppression and assaulting the women's private parts as a weapon to prevent women from taking part in the protest, she said. During the interaction, Raja also referred to the presence of Ankita Bhandari's parents at the protest. Meanwhile, the Delhi Police have registered multiple FIRs for alleged violations of prohibitory orders imposed in Connaught Place and other parts of New Delhi during protests on Friday, officials said on Saturday. According to police officials, announcements were repeatedly made asking people not to assemble, but a crowd gathered around Connaught Place. Police said FIRs would be registered for violations of prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and action would also be taken against repeat offenders. The action follows a Tiranga rally held by protesters outside Central Park in Connaught Place on Friday amid heightened security. Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) workers and supporters also gathered to hold a Tiranga rally, directing their protest against the Election Commission over alleged irregularities in the electoral process. In a related development, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke, who was detained by Delhi Police ahead of the planned 'Lehra Do Tiranga' rally in the national capital, will be produced before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) at Mandir Marg Police Station around 12 pm on Saturday, his legal counsel said. In a post on social media platform X, advocate Ratna Singh said, He will be produced before SEM Mandir Marg PS around 12 PM. Police placed Dipke under preventive detention at his residence in New Delhi on Friday, invoking prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS. CJP representatives alleged that he was taken to an undisclosed location without immediate access to his lawyers. The detention came amid heightened security arrangements and restrictions on public gatherings in parts of the national capital following protests over the electoral revision process and demands for action against the Election Commission. (ANI)
